newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks rebound at opening.
newsitem.headline: French stocks rebound at opening.

text.p: French stocks rebounded at Friday's opening after three days of decline but the market was expected to remain cautious ahead of U.S. jobs figures due in the afternoon.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 13.42 points, or 0.57 percent, at 2,528.84 at 0845 GMT, while the CAC-40 April futures contract was 11 points higher at 2,527.

Thomson-CSF shares fell 2.59 percent to 188 francs. The Figaro newspaper said the government would not accept Britain's GEC as a candidate to take over the state's 58 percent stake. The Finance Ministry declined comment.

Generale des Eaux shares rose 2.6 percent to 753 francs after an analysts' meeting on Friday morning. The company said on Thursday it returned to profit in 1996 with net attributable profit of 1.95 billion francs, compared with a loss of 3.69 billion for the preceding year.

Eridania Beghin-Say shares were up 3.29 percent at 878 francs. After the bourse close on Thursday, it reported net attributable profit of 1.66 billion francs for 1996, up from 1.53 billion for the preceding year.
